description: An original, jurisdiction-neutral lighting vendor access, work coordination, and accountable sign-out record for an indoor, exterior, emergency, or egress lighting system whose fixtures, circuits, supports, controls, illumination, and electrical condition must be traceable. It connects facility identity, asset-specific evidence, hazards, qualified decisions, exceptions, service status, and accountable closeout without replacing employer procedures or trade judgment.

blocks.label: Record reference and timing
Facility, location, and responsible parties

blocks.guidance: This Lighting record organizes facts and evidence. It does not replace employer energy-control procedures, permits, manufacturer instructions, required inspection, emergency response, or qualified trade judgment. Stop and route any unsafe or uncertain condition.
blocks.label: Safety and authority boundary

sections.guidance: Open one traceable record, identify the responsible parties, and set the review route.
sections.title: Lighting Vendor Sign-In identity and routing

blocks.label: Lighting asset and system profile

blocks.guidance: Check only directly observed or source-supported items; explain inaccessible, not applicable, or conflicting evidence below.
items: Zone, circuit, panel, control, fixture, and served-area identities reconcile
Fixture housing, lens, diffuser, door, gasket, fasteners, and supports are observed
Lamp, LED module, driver, ballast, socket, connector, and wiring condition are recorded
Heat, discoloration, odor, arcing, buzzing, flicker, and intermittent operation are documented
Grounding, bonding, enclosure, cover, strain relief, and conductor protection are observed
Occupancy sensor, timer, photocell, dimmer, relay, contactor, and BAS status are reconciled
Emergency unit, exit sign, battery, charger, indicator, and transfer evidence is linked
Illumination complaint, dark area, glare, color, flicker, and task impact are recorded
Water intrusion, condensation, corrosion, dirt, insect, and environmental exposure are documented
Ladder, lift, ceiling, overhead, traffic, and falling-object access conditions are controlled
Lamp and material type, compatibility, disposal, and replacement evidence are recorded
Open circuit, fixture, emergency-lighting, and occupant-impact deficiencies are assigned

blocks.guidance: Tie each entry to a location, source, reading condition, photo, tag, log, or other retrievable evidence.

blocks.guidance: A checked item confirms the control was addressed; it does not substitute for the referenced procedure, permit, test, or source.
items: Vendor identity, employer, contact, work order, and authorized scope reconcile
Required license, credential, training, insurance, and site orientation are confirmed
Work area, route, escort, keys, badges, doors, alarms, and restricted spaces are defined
Host and vendor exchange energy-control procedures and affected-system status
Permits, hot work, confined space, roof, lift, electrical, chemical, or shutdown controls are routed
Tools, materials, parts, chemicals, cylinders, devices, and waste entering the site are traceable
Scope change, unsafe condition, damage, alarm, spill, or service interruption triggers stop and host contact
Sign-out reconciles people, access items, locks, tags, tools, materials, waste, work status, and handoff

blocks.guidance: A checked condition requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.
items: Exposed live parts, arcing, burning, smoke, melted insulation, or severe heat is present
Wet electrical equipment, water intrusion, condensation, or conductive contamination is unresolved
Fixture, lens, support, pole, mast arm, ceiling, or mounting could fall or detach
Emergency, exit, stair, life-safety, or required egress illumination may be unavailable
Ladder, lift, ceiling, traffic, roof, weather, or overhead-work access is unsafe
Hazardous-location, voltage, lamp, driver, ballast, or control compatibility is uncertain
Required de-energization, lockout, qualified electrical work, or outage authorization is absent
Field status conflicts with circuit schedules, controls, test records, or emergency-power evidence

blocks.guidance: Do not resolve a checked stop condition by inference, an unchecked box, or a generic sign-off. Preserve the condition, protective action, authority, evidence, owner, due point, and verified disposition.
blocks.label: Escalation record boundary

sections.guidance: Stop when authority, access, energy control, safety, evidence, or service status is unresolved.
sections.title: Lighting stop conditions, exceptions, and escalation

blocks.label: Vendor Sign-In decision, timing, and authority

blocks.guidance: Check only controls supported by referenced evidence; unresolved controls remain open conditions.
items: Facility host confirms vendor identity, authorization, scope, area, and schedule
Qualified owners approve energy, electrical, fire, roof, confined-space, and shutdown controls
Scope changes are approved before new work, equipment, material, or area access
Access credentials, keys, locks, tags, permits, and temporary devices retain clear custody
Work status and any incomplete or unsafe condition are accepted at sign-out
Vendor and facility contacts receive the same restriction, owner, and next action
Qualified electrical reviewer approves energized testing, circuit work, and return to service
Emergency and egress lighting status is independently verified where applicable
Fixture, lamp, driver, ballast, voltage, control, and environment compatibility is documented
Dark-area, glare, accessibility, traffic, and occupant impacts have controls and owners
Temporary lighting and any circuit restriction have a due point and removal trigger
Controls, schedules, sensors, dimming, and BAS commands are restored to the approved state

blocks.guidance: Do not use this Lighting record as permission for work outside the approved scope, as proof that an unperformed test passed, or as a substitute for required qualified-person, employer, authority, or manufacturer approval.

blocks.guidance: Unchecked items require an exception disposition or a documented reopen trigger before the record can be treated as closed.
items: Fixtures, lenses, diffusers, covers, supports, panels, and ceilings are restored
Circuit, control, sensor, timer, photocell, dimming, and BAS status are documented
Emergency and exit units have required functional evidence and clear indicators
Ladders, lifts, barriers, lamps, packaging, debris, and regulated waste have final custody
Illumination, flicker, glare, dark-area, and occupant complaints have a final disposition
Parts, circuit records, photos, test evidence, restrictions, and next service are filed
